description: Keyframe animation data for 12 PDB molecules — scientifically grounded biotech visualization

molecules.name: Crambin
molecules.description: 46-residue plant seed protein; one of the highest-resolution crystal structures ever solved

hero_moment.description: Pull-back from the tightly packed disulfide core to reveal the full fold — three disulfide bonds holding a tiny protein like rivets

molecules.name: B-DNA Dodecamer
molecules.description: Classic B-form DNA double helix; the Dickerson-Drew dodecamer d(CGCGAATTCGCG)

hero_moment.description: Camera tracks along the helix axis end-on, revealing the 36-degree twist per base pair and the deep major groove

molecules.name: Hemoglobin
molecules.description: Adult human hemoglobin (alpha2beta2 tetramer) in the deoxy T-state; exhibits allosteric cooperativity

hero_moment.description: Fade out alpha subunits to expose beta subunits and the central cavity — then sweep up to show the quaternary symmetry of the full tetramer

molecules.name: ATP Synthase (F1Fo)
molecules.description: Mitochondrial ATP synthase; rotary molecular motor driven by proton gradient across the inner membrane

hero_moment.description: Camera locks on the c-ring from below the membrane plane and watches the 10-subunit ring spin, then pulls back through the membrane bilayer to reveal the full F1Fo assembly towering above

molecules.name: SARS-CoV-2 Main Protease (Mpro)
molecules.description: COVID-19 main protease; homodimeric cysteine protease critical for viral polyprotein processing

hero_moment.description: Fly into the substrate-binding cleft at speed, brake hard at the catalytic dyad, and watch the Cys145 thiolate glow as the active site comes into focus

molecules.name: Green Fluorescent Protein (GFP)
molecules.description: Aequorea victoria GFP; beta-barrel protecting the autocatalytic chromophore Ser65-Tyr66-Gly67

hero_moment.description: Ghost the beta-barrel to near-transparency and watch the chromophore pulse green from inside its protective cage — then fade the barrel back in around it

molecules.name: Insulin Hexamer
molecules.description: Zinc-coordinated T6 insulin hexamer; storage form in pancreatic beta cells, dissociates to active monomer

hero_moment.description: Spin the hexamer on its 3-fold axis and then trigger the morph — watch 6 chains slowly drift apart as zinc coordination dissolves and active monomers escape

molecules.name: p53-DNA Complex
molecules.description: Tumor suppressor p53 tetrameric DNA-binding domain bound to a 20-bp response element; guardian of the genome

hero_moment.description: Zoom into the DNA major groove where the L3 loop inserts — camera sweeps along the DNA axis revealing all four p53 monomers embracing the response element like a clamp

molecules.name: Glutamine Synthetase
molecules.description: Bacterial Glutamine Synthetase; dodecameric enzyme (two hexameric rings) catalysing ATP-dependent glutamine synthesis

hero_moment.description: View from directly above the symmetry axis — 6 active sites form a ring of orange glows as ATP substrates are shown binding simultaneously, then pull back to reveal the two stacked rings

molecules.name: OmpF Porin
molecules.description: E. coli outer membrane porin OmpF; homotrimeric beta-barrel channel controlling ion passage across the outer membrane

hero_moment.description: Slice through the membrane horizontally to expose all three channel pores simultaneously — then animate ion particles flowing downward through the L3 constriction zone in single file

molecules.name: Adenylate Kinase
molecules.description: Adenylate kinase (AK1); paradigmatic enzyme showing large-scale open-to-closed domain motion upon substrate binding

hero_moment.description: Slow-motion open-to-closed clamp motion — the AMPbind domain swings down from the left and the ATPlid clamps from the right, burying the substrates; hold closed for 1 second then reopen

molecules.name: CRISPR-Cas9
molecules.description: SpCas9 in complex with sgRNA and target DNA; RNA-guided endonuclease creating a DSB 3 bp upstream of the PAM

hero_moment.description: Ghost the NUC lobe to transparency revealing the RNA-DNA heteroduplex inside; trigger the HNH domain snap-to-cleavage with a red flash at the DSB site — the molecular scissors close

molecules.name: Ubiquitin
molecules.description: 76-residue eukaryotic regulatory protein; the universal protein-degradation tag and beta-grasp fold archetype

hero_moment.description: Zoom to Lys48 — the poly-ubiquitin chain linkage site that marks proteins for 26S proteasomal degradation; gentle rotation reveals the compact beta-grasp fold (beta1-loop-beta2-alpha1-beta3-beta4-alpha2-beta5)

molecules.name: Hen Egg-White Lysozyme
molecules.description: 129-residue antimicrobial enzyme; the first enzyme structure solved by X-ray crystallography and a classical model for protein folding studies

hero_moment.description: Classic orbit revealing the deep cleft between the alpha (helical) and beta (sheet) domains, then zoom to the Glu35/Asp52 catalytic dyad that cleaves the glycosidic bond in bacterial cell wall peptidoglycan via general acid-base catalysis

molecules.name: Sperm Whale Myoglobin
molecules.description: 153-residue oxygen-storage hemoprotein; the first protein structure ever solved by X-ray crystallography (Kendrew 1958), earning the Nobel Prize in Chemistry 1962

hero_moment.description: Historical first-ever protein structure reveal — sequential illumination of the eight alpha helices (A-H) as Kendrew first traced them in 1957, then dive into the heme pocket showing iron coordination by proximal His93 and the distal His64 oxygen-binding site

molecules.name: HIV-1 Protease
molecules.description: Homodimeric aspartyl protease essential for HIV maturation; landmark antiretroviral target that ushered in structure-based drug design for viral diseases

hero_moment.description: Flap opening/closing morph showing the two beta-hairpin flaps gating active site access, followed by 180-degree rotation around the C2 axis to demonstrate perfect homodimer symmetry — both monomers contributing Asp25 to form the catalytic dyad

molecules.name: EGFR Kinase Domain
molecules.description: Epidermal growth factor receptor tyrosine kinase domain; key oncogenic driver mutated in lung adenocarcinoma and the target of erlotinib, gefitinib, and osimertinib

hero_moment.description: Dive into the ATP-binding cleft occupied by erlotinib, revealing the hinge-region hydrogen bonds (Met769); pull back to show the activation loop in its DFG-in active conformation contrasted with DFG-out inactive state

molecules.name: Cytochrome P450 3A4
molecules.description: The dominant human drug-metabolizing CYP enzyme responsible for clearing ~50% of all clinical drugs; remarkable promiscuous active site that can accommodate multiple substrates simultaneously

hero_moment.description: Fly-through of the massive ~1400 cubic Angstrom active site cavity — among the largest of any CYP — showing how multiple drug molecules can bind simultaneously; the flexible F-G loop (residues 210-245) gates substrate access and adopts an open conformation here

molecules.name: PD-L1 Checkpoint Protein
molecules.description: Programmed death-ligand 1; the immunosuppressive checkpoint protein targeted by pembrolizumab, atezolizumab, and other blockbuster immuno-oncology drugs

hero_moment.description: Zoom to checkpoint binding interface showing the flat hydrophobic surface where PD-1 docks; key contact residues (Tyr56, Glu58, Arg113, Met115) highlighted where pembrolizumab's CDR loops bury to competitively block the immunosuppressive PD-1/PD-L1 interaction

molecules.name: Beta-2 Adrenergic Receptor
molecules.description: Archetypal GPCR; the first non-rhodopsin GPCR structure and template for understanding the ~35% of marketed drugs that target GPCRs. Kobilka & Lefkowitz Nobel Prize 2012

hero_moment.description: Transmembrane helix bundle rotation — top-down view showing ligand buried deep in the 7TM core; then rotate to intracellular face revealing the G-protein coupling cavity formed by outward movement of TM6

molecules.name: KcsA Potassium Channel
molecules.description: Bacterial K+ channel from Streptomyces lividans; MacKinnon's Nobel Prize 2003 structure establishing the selectivity filter mechanism for K+ permeation over Na+

hero_moment.description: Top-down axial view into the 4-fold symmetric ion pathway; zoom to TVGYG selectivity filter showing K+ ions in single-file at sites S1-S4 and the carbonyl oxygen cage that mimics the ion's water coordination shell — explaining 1000-fold K+/Na+ selectivity

molecules.name: Phenylalanine tRNA
molecules.description: Transfer RNA carrying phenylalanine; the first tRNA crystal structure, revealing the universal L-shaped tertiary fold that all cytoplasmic tRNAs adopt for ribosome decoding

hero_moment.description: Rotate to reveal the L-shape from the side — acceptor stem (3'-CCA amino acid attachment) at one tip and anticodon loop at the other, 75 Angstroms apart; the L-shape positions these two functional sites for simultaneous interaction with the ribosome A-site

molecules.name: Nucleosome Core Particle
molecules.description: 146 bp of DNA wrapped 1.65 turns around a histone octamer (H2A/H2B/H3/H4)2; the fundamental packaging unit of eukaryotic chromatin and the substrate of histone-modifying enzymes

hero_moment.description: Zoom out from the histone octamer core to reveal the full 1.65-turn left-handed DNA superhelix; then highlight the intrinsically disordered histone tails (H3 Lys4/Lys9/Lys27, H4 Lys16) protruding outward as the epigenetic code platforms

molecules.name: GroEL-GroES Chaperonin
molecules.description: The bacterial Hsp60 chaperonin machine; a ~1 MDa bullet-shaped assembly that uses ATP-driven cavity expansion to provide an isolated folding chamber for misfolded proteins up to ~60 kDa

hero_moment.description: Side cut-away style zoom revealing the internal folding cavity — the cis ring capped by GroES dome showing the ~80,000 cubic Angstrom Anfinsen cage where a substrate protein folds in isolation, shielded from aggregation-prone neighbors

molecules.name: 26S Proteasome
molecules.description: The ~2.5 MDa ATP-dependent protease that degrades poly-ubiquitinated proteins; the validated cancer drug target of bortezomib and carfilzomib, and the endpoint of the ubiquitin pathway

hero_moment.description: Top-down into the 20S catalytic barrel flanked by two 19S regulatory caps; zoom through the 13-Angstrom gated pore — opened by Rpt subunit C-terminal tails — into the inner chamber where six threonine protease active sites line the beta-ring wall

molecules.name: RNA Polymerase II
molecules.description: Eukaryotic mRNA-synthesizing enzyme; the ~500 kDa 12-subunit machine responsible for transcribing all protein-coding genes. Kornberg Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2006

hero_moment.description: Zoom into the active site channel — the cleft between Rpb1 and Rpb2 where the DNA-RNA hybrid sits at the catalytic Mg2+ (Metal A); then reveal the RNA exit tunnel threading under the clamp domain toward the mRNA cap-addition machinery

molecules.name: IgG1 Antibody
molecules.description: Full-length immunoglobulin G1; the most abundant serum antibody class and the molecular scaffold for virtually all approved therapeutic monoclonal antibodies

hero_moment.description: Y-shape reveal with hinge flex — the two Fab arms pivot ±20 degrees at the flexible hinge while the Fc stem remains anchored; zoom to one Fab tip highlighting the six CDR loops (L1-L3, H1-H3) that form the antigen-binding paratope

molecules.name: SARS-CoV-2 Spike Protein
molecules.description: Trimeric class-I fusion protein in prefusion open conformation; the target of all approved COVID-19 vaccines and the key determinant of variant immune escape

hero_moment.description: RBD flip-up from closed prefusion trimer to open ACE2-binding conformation; zoom to the receptor-binding motif (residues 484-505) where Omicron/Delta escape mutations cluster, showing how a 62-degree rotation of RBD exposes the ACE2-binding ridge

molecules.name: Beta2AR-Gs Protein Complex
molecules.description: The first structure of a GPCR coupled to its heterotrimeric G protein; reveals the molecular basis of transmembrane signal transduction — from agonist binding to GDP/GTP exchange. Nobel Prize 2012

hero_moment.description: Exploded view separating receptor and G protein to reveal the coupling interface; the outward swing of TM6 (14-Angstrom movement) opens the intracellular cavity for Galpha alpha5 helix insertion, displacing GDP and triggering the GEF reaction

molecules.name: Collagen Triple Helix
molecules.description: Archetypal collagen Gly-Pro-Hyp repeat peptide in triple-helix form; the most abundant structural protein in the human body (~30% of total protein mass) and basis of connective tissue disorders

hero_moment.description: Axial spin revealing the 7/2 supercoil — three polyproline-II helices coiling around a common axis like a rope; each chain offset by one residue, Gly at every third position threading into the sterically constrained central core, and hydroxyproline stabilizing via water-mediated H-bonds

molecules.name: F-Actin Filament
molecules.description: Filamentous actin in the barbed-end elongating state; the ~8-nm diameter polar helical filament that drives muscle contraction, cell migration, and endocytosis via myosin and nucleator interactions

hero_moment.description: Zoom along the barbed (plus) end where ATP-actin subunits incorporate at ~10 subunits/s; the two-start left-handed genetic helix visible as a twisting double braid with 166-Angstrom crossover repeat and 166-degree twist per subunit — the geometry exploited by cofilin severing

molecules.name: Streptavidin-Biotin
molecules.description: Homotetrameric biotin-binding protein with the tightest known non-covalent interaction (Kd ~10-14 M); the workhorse of biotechnology labeling, ELISA, SPR, and biosensor assays worldwide

hero_moment.description: Zoom into one of the four equivalent biotin pockets showing the Trp cage (Trp79, Trp92, Trp108, Trp120) closing around biotin; the L3,4 loop snapping shut contributes ~75% of binding energy via van der Waals contacts on biotin's thiophane ring

molecules.name: Cas12a (Cpf1) with crRNA
molecules.description: Class-2 type-V CRISPR nuclease with crRNA guide; creates staggered 5-nt 5'-overhangs and processes its own pre-crRNA, making it preferred for multiplex gene editing with a single RNase III

hero_moment.description: Crescent orbit showing the bilobed architecture with crRNA threading through the central channel; highlight the PAM-interacting domain (TTTV PAM) and seed region where target DNA is interrogated; then show RuvC and Nuc domains positioned to create the 5-nt 5'-overhang DSB

molecules.name: Kinesin-1 Motor Domain
molecules.description: Processive microtubule-based motor protein; walks hand-over-hand toward microtubule plus ends with 8-nm steps coupled to ATP hydrolysis, transporting organelles and mRNA granules in axons

hero_moment.description: Power stroke morph — neck linker docking animation showing the 12-residue neck linker (Ile325-Lys336) snapping from disordered to ordered beta-strand alongside the motor core upon ATP binding, generating the mechanical stroke that propels cargo 8 nm toward the microtubule plus end

molecules.name: Taq DNA Polymerase
molecules.description: Thermostable DNA polymerase from Thermus aquaticus; the enzyme that made PCR practical by surviving 95-degree denaturation cycles, transforming molecular biology, diagnostics, and forensics

hero_moment.description: Orbit of the right-hand fold showing thumb (residues 507-632), palm (419-506), and fingers (533-560) domains; morph of thumb closing around DNA template-primer during nucleotide incorporation; zoom to the two-Mg2+ (Asp610, Asp785) SN2 phosphoryl transfer mechanism

molecules.name: p53 DNA-Binding Domain
molecules.description: The core domain of the guardian of the genome; mutated in ~50% of all human cancers at six major hotspot residues, making it the most frequently mutated tumor suppressor in cancer

hero_moment.description: Zoom to the zinc coordination loop — Cys176, His179, Cys238, Cys242 tetrahedrally coordinating a single Zn2+ that scaffolds L2 and L3 loops onto the DNA-contact surface; highlight L2/L3 making major-groove contacts via Arg248 and Arg273, the two most frequently mutated residues in human cancer
